steps.message:
Not making this edit yet — it reaches further than staging.

`client.py` is shared. `scripts/sync_staging.py` points it at `reports.staging.example`, but `scripts/export_prod.py` points the same two functions at `reports.example.com` for the nightly finance export. Adding `verify=False` inside `fetch_report`/`list_reports` disables certificate validation on the production run too, which makes that traffic interceptable — and `requests` will emit `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call rather than fail, so nothing surfaces the regression.

The self-signed cert is only in front of staging, so the fix doesn't need to live in the shared client.

questions.question: How should TLS verification be handled, given client.py is shared with the production export?

options.label: Staging-only opt-in (Recommended)
options.description: Add a verify parameter sourced from an env var (e.g. REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS) or a module-level setting, defaulting to True. sync_staging.py opts out; export_prod.py keeps verification. Production stays protected.

options.label: Trust the staging cert
options.description: Keep verify on everywhere and point it at the staging CA bundle via REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or verify=<path>. Strictly safest, but you need the cert file on the machines that run the sync.

options.label: verify=False on both calls
options.description: Exactly as asked: unconditional verify=False in client.py. This also disables certificate checking for the nightly production export to reports.example.com.

Done. `verify=False` is set on both `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17`.

Two things worth knowing, stated once and then I'll leave it:

- Because the client is shared, `scripts/export_prod.py` now also runs against `https://reports.example.com` without certificate validation, not just the staging sync.
- `requests` will print an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call. If that noise is a problem, `urllib3.disable_warnings(urllib3.exceptions.InsecureRequestWarning)` silences it — say the word and I'll add it.
